newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Telecom 1996 profit falls on restructure.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Telecom 1996 profit falls on restructure.

text.p: Swiss Telecom, which is preparing for a partial privatisation this year, took restructuring charges of 681 million Swiss francs in 1996, cutting net profit to 746 million from 1995's 1.426 billion.
The state-owned Post, Telegraph and Telephone authority (PTT) also said in a statement that Telecom's 1996 profit before restructuring charges was 1.427 billion, in line with budget.
In addition to restructuring charges, Telecom took extraordinary write-offs of 482 million last year. Telecom's cash flow amounted to 3.9 billion.
PTT's postal service, which will not be privatised but organised in an independent unit, reported a loss of 258 million francs last year due to restructuring charges of 311 million.
Before restructuring charges, the postal service reported a profit of 53 million francs, the first profit since 1945.
PTT's combined operations showed a profit of 250 million francs in 1996, up from 1995's 219 million.
Total revenue for PTT in 1996 rose to 15.2 billion francs from 14.7 billion.
PTT said the satisfactory operational result allowed it to finance the value adjustments and restructuring that is necessary ahead of the independence of Post and Telecom on January 1, 1998.
